path.writeTimings: turn_start (one row appended), turn_end (one row appended), any lane change (P1: push / drain / restore), clean shutdown

purpose.kept: the two facts the log cannot express: WHO was running (pid/boot_id/clean_shutdown) and WHICH turn was open (open_turn)
purpose.notKept: everything derivable from cli-main.jsonl (turn counter, history, last outcome) — the log stays the single source of truth (K4)
purpose.neverWritten: the sidecar never rewrites a log row; the only repair is ONE appended turn_end{outcome:"interrupted"}, recorded in repaired[]

failureSemantics.missing: no checkpoint: recovery does not touch the log at all (a dangling turn_start may belong to another live process)
failureSemantics.unparsable: the WHOLE file is ignored + observed on stderr; behaviour is exactly 'missing' (never read as a clean exit)
failureSemantics.sessionMismatch: ignored + observed: the sidecar was copied/renamed and cannot describe this directory
failureSemantics.writeFailure: reported on stderr and swallowed: checkpointing is observation and can never fail a turn

open_turn.meaning: the turn THIS process started and has not closed yet (null = no turn is open)
open_turn.repairCondition: open_turn.id has a turn_start row in cli-main.jsonl AND no turn_end row for that id (double signature)
open_turn.idempotency: the second boot sees the appended turn_end and only clears open_turn: the log is byte-identical (assertion A2)

clean_shutdown.true: the process left through Runtime.shutdown(); the next boot repairs NOTHING, whatever the log looks like
clean_shutdown.false: written by every activity (turn_start, turn_end); a crash therefore leaves the last value false

version.description: sidecar schema version (NOT a data-file format version; any other value voids the file)

session.description: "<workspace>/<session>" self-description; a mismatch voids the file

boot_id.description: one id per process start (process-wide constant)

updated_at.description: unix seconds of the last write

last_outcome.description: redundant with the log (operator convenience); the log wins on any conflict

log_write_errors.description: PersistentSessionLog.writeErrorCount() sampled at every write; non-zero means disk and memory diverged

lanes.description: E §1.3 P1 ① (W787): the two injection lanes exactly as the inbox holds them — a message that was ACCEPTED and not yet injected. Written on every lane change (push / drain), so a crash loses at most the newest change (G1-4: a user's message used to vanish silently). Restoring is deliberately silent: a message queued by a dead process was already announced by it.

delivered_ids.description: E §1.3 P1 ① (W787): the bounded (512, oldest-first) ledger of injection ids this session already ACCEPTED. It is the cross-process half of the idempotency key (capability 2's `receipt:<wid>:<attempt>`), so a receipt replayed after a restart is still dropped as a duplicate (B3).

repaired.description: every log row THIS engine appended for recovery; empty on a healthy session (assertion A2: length stays 1 after a second boot)

source.description: the delivery envelope (kind / form / sender), verbatim
